original_value: Dynamic high resolution data on human population distribution is of great importance for a wide spectrum of activities and real-life applications, but is too difficult and expensive to obtain directly. Therefore, generating fine-scaled population distributions from coarse population data is of great significance. However, there are three major challenges: 1) the complexity in spatial relations between high and low resolution population; 2) the dependence of population distributions on other external information; 3) the difficulty in retrieving temporal distribution patterns. In this paper, we first propose the idea to generate dynamic population distributions in full-time series, then we design dynamic population mapping via deep neural network(DeepDPM), a model that describes both spatial and temporal patterns using coarse data and point of interest information. In DeepDPM, we utilize super-resolution convolutional neural network(SRCNN) based model to directly map coarse data into higher resolution data, and a timeembedded long short-term memory model to effectively capture the periodicity nature to smooth the finer-scaled results from the previous static SRCNN model. We perform extensive experiments on a real-life mobile dataset collected from Shanghai. Our results demonstrate that DeepDPM outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods and a suite of frequent data-mining approaches. Moreover, DeepDPM breaks through the limitation from previous works in time dimension so that dynamic predictions in all-day time slots can be obtained.

result.paraphrase: Dynamic high-resolution human population distribution data is crucial for many activities and real-world applications, yet it is too costly and difficult to collect directly. As a result, producing fine-grained population distributions from coarse population data is highly significant. Three main challenges remain: 1) the complexity of spatial relationships between high- and low-resolution population data; 2) the dependence of population distributions on other external information; and 3) the difficulty of extracting temporal distribution patterns. In this paper, we first propose generating dynamic population distributions as full time series, and then introduce dynamic population mapping via a deep neural network (DeepDPM), which models both spatial and temporal patterns using coarse data and point-of-interest information. Within DeepDPM, a super-resolution convolutional neural network (SRCNN)-based model is used to directly map coarse data to higher-resolution data, while a time-embedded long short-term memory model effectively captures periodicity to smooth the finer-grained results from the earlier static SRCNN model. We conduct extensive experiments on a real-world mobile dataset collected in Shanghai. The results show that DeepDPM outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods and a range of frequent data-mining approaches. In addition, DeepDPM overcomes the temporal limitation of previous work, enabling dynamic predictions for all-day time slots.
